name: Edelweiss Lodge
blurbs: The pass is closed, the phone line is down, and someone at the lodge has very cold blood.
Eight guests, one blizzard and a weekend that nobody will ever forget.
Hot chocolate, a roaring blaze and a body that went cold long before morning.
By the time the snowploughs arrive, the lodge will have one guest fewer.
The snow has buried the road, the lights keep flickering, and one guest is never going home.
Fresh powder on the slopes, mulled wine by the fire, and a quarrel that ended in murder.
Nobody can leave the lodge until the storm passes, and somebody is counting on it.
A ski champion, an old rival and a long night that only one of them survived.
The season's last guests are checking in, and one of them has no intention of checking out.
The lodge has a guest book, a locked door and a host who never takes a day off.
High in the valley, old friends share a bottle, a story and one very old secret.
The view is breathtaking. So, it turns out, is the company.
motives: the lodge had been left to the wrong side of the family
a skiing accident twenty winters ago had never been an accident
the avalanche report had been signed by the wrong person
a promise made on the summit had been broken on the way down
the gold in the old mine shaft was real after all
the rescue that made a local hero had never happened the way it was told
the lodge's guest book recorded a visit that someone had sworn never took place
a rope had been cut on a climb many years ago
the new ski lift would run straight through a family's land
a missing guide's last letter had finally been delivered
an Olympic medal had been won with someone else's time
the mountain hut's old debts had been passed down with the keys
a broken engagement had cost one guest far more than a ring
the insurance on the lodge paid out only if it lost its owner
an old map showed who had really owned the slopes
epilogues: {murderer} and {victim} were the only two in the {area} while the storm hammered the shutters. When the snow stopped, only {murderer} came out, because {motive}.
Nobody else went into the {area} that night. {murderer} made sure of it: {motive}.
The {area} had two people in it when the lights flickered. {murderer} had a reason older than the lodge itself: {motive}.
The wind covered every sound from the {area}. {murderer} had spent many winters waiting for {victim} to come back here: {motive}.
Everyone else was by the fire when {victim} went to the {area}. {murderer} followed, because {motive}.
{murderer} was first to raise the alarm, which was generous, since only {murderer} had been in the {area} with {victim}: {motive}.
Up here, a quarrel can wait for years. In the {area} it finally could not: {motive}.
By morning there was no trace of anyone leaving the {area}, as {murderer} knew there would not be. The reason went back a long way: {motive}.
